The test image shows a tomato leaf with numerous small, dark brown/black spots scattered across the surface, with some yellowing. Spots are small and circular. Top candidates: Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato, Early_Blight.

Let me view reference images for the top candidates first.
This Septoria Leaf Blotch reference looks very similar to the test image. Let me check Bacterial Speck and a few other classes.
Bacterial Speck shows larger, darker spots on a green leaf — less similar. Let me check Early Blight and Leaf Mold.
Not matching — Early Blight shows large lesions on whole plant. Let me check Leaf Mold.
Leaf Mold doesn't match — different leaf shape and no discrete spots. Let me check Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus and Powdery Mildew.
Powdery Mildew shows white patches — not matching. Let me check Late Blight and one more Septoria reference.
Microscopic image, not useful for comparison. Let me check the second Septoria reference and one more class.
Let me check one more class — Cucumber Mosaic Virus — to complete the spread.

I've now covered 8 different classes. Summary of comparisons:

- **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch** (CDDM_1006): Nearly identical — same rounded leaf, same yellowing, same small dark circular spots scattered uniformly. Gray background matches too.
- **Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato**: Larger, more irregular spots on dark green leaf — not matching.
- **Early_Blight**: Large necrotic lesions, whole-plant view — not matching.
- **Leaf_Mold**: Different leaf shape, no discrete spots.
- **TSWV**: Different spot pattern and leaf color.
- **Powdery_Mildew**: White powdery patches — not matching.
- **Late_Blight**: Microscopic reference — not comparable.
- **Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus**: Leaf distortion/curling — not matching.

The test image is a near-perfect visual match to Septoria Leaf Blotch reference CDDM_1006.jpg: same rounded leaf shape, same yellowing, same small dark circular spots scattered uniformly.
